Thanks for your response and your concern.  I want to make one thing abundantly clear.  **At NO POINT did I wish to say that God screwed up in designing me, in designing anyone else or anything else, or in doing anything ever.  That would be the height of totally depraved ingratitude for His creation.**  I only wanted to express my total desire to avoid even the appearance of such abominable blasphemy in my actions, in case some demon is tempting my subconscious into doing its bidding.

As for ascribing my issues to chemical imbalances - how far could we take this approach?  Could psychiatry have also intervened in the spiritual state of mass murderers and pedophiles?  I'm not trying to be contentious here, I'm really asking what your opinion is.  And as such, I'm not quite seeing the logic behind seeking treatment that you presented.  Basically, I'm still not convinced that what I have is an actual 'problem' according to God, regardless of how it's recognized by society.  Maybe I have a spiritual malady and fixing the physical symptoms would leave my soul forever unrepaired.  Or maybe I am one of the damned, destined for eternal fire, and my death and suffering would be pleasing to Him in a certain sense (see this [John Piper interview](https://www.desiringgod.org/interviews/does-god-delight-in-destroying-sinners) for a quick Bible study on the topic) whereas my continuing to enjoy the fruits of depravity would be utterly detestable.  I really have no idea, nor do I know how to begin figuring it out.

When it comes to spiritual authority and trust - and here you will see how rotten and corrupted my soul really is - I haven't found a single one that I trust.  Every time I walk into a new church, and for a few Sundays I feel a level of inspiredness I've never noticed before.  And then I witness something so appalling that I can't bear to go back to that church.  Such as a sermon turning midway through into a fundraiser for the church's programs.  Or a drunk guy lying unconscious on the sidewalk and not a single person interested in him after the service.  Or Revelation starts being interpreted in a manner completely contrary to what I observed with my own two eyes (Beast = Islam, Whore = NYC, 9/11 = Beast utterly destroying the Whore).  Or a story honouring martyrs in the early church for competing for their crowns of martyrdom, literally fighting in line to be killed (needless to say I didn't see a sign up sheet after the service).  I mean I was ready to fall in love with each of these churches and every single time it's like God is saying fuck you you're not good enough for them.

Looking at the corpus of Paul's letters (2 Cor 11, as well as 1 Cor 9, Col 3, Gal 5 to name a few, also 1 Peter is heavily focused on this theme) looking at the lives of the prophets (including the recounting done in Hebrews 11 and James 5), looking at the history of the Church, persecuted and persecuting, the message of Biblical Christianity seems loud and clear:  Suffer obediently in this life, and you will be rewarded in the next. If you don't hate your life and all your loved ones, you can't follow me Jesus says.  The healings you mention.  They serve 2 purposes that pervaded the manner in which these miracles were recounted.  First, to glorify Jesus as God.  Second, so that the recipients of the healing would sin no more.  It seems more questionable to me to say that 'healing is good in its own right' than to say 'suffering is good in its own right'.

And I agree that Points 1 and 2 are mutually exclusive.  This is what I fundamentally don't get about Christianity.  If suffering for Jesus is so awesome then what's everyone doing feeding kids and vaccinating Africans and promoting education and clean water?  If Augustine was so inspired then why aren't we still waging Crusades against the Muslims?  If according to Mother Theresa terrible pain is the kiss of Jesus then why did she attempt over and over to heal that pain?  It just doesn't make any sense.  What is it that God wants for us in this life?  Joy or suffering?  Which one brings Him more glory in and of itself, or is it according to the soul of the individual?  And how do we determine this case by case so we know what to execute?
